questions.q: How does this lesson define reference data?
options: Any data stored in a relational database table
A small, stable, finite list of valid values used to classify or constrain other data
A backup copy of master data kept for disaster recovery
The full set of a customer's past orders
questions.explain: Reference data is the controlled vocabulary — like country codes or status codes — that other data is classified against, distinct from master data (entities) and transactional data (events).

questions.q: What is the standard 'shape' most reference data follows, per this lesson?
options: A full paragraph of narrative description for every value
A numeric score with no accompanying text
A single free-text field with no structure
A short code paired with a human-readable description, plus control fields like an active flag
questions.explain: The code (e.g., 'US') is what systems store and compare; the description (e.g., 'United States') is what a person reads — the same pattern applies whether the list has 5 or 5,000 values.

questions.q: What distinguishes external reference data from internal reference data?
options: There is no meaningful distinction between the two
External reference data is defined by an outside standards body; internal reference data is defined entirely by the organization
External reference data never changes, while internal reference data changes daily
Internal reference data is always larger than external reference data
questions.explain: ISO country codes are an example of external reference data the organization adopts and synchronizes with; order-status codes are internal, defined and governed entirely by the business itself.

questions.q: Using the 'practical test' from this lesson, which of these is reference data rather than master data or transactional data?
options: The full list of customers who have ever placed an order
A customer's complete purchase history
The list of valid order-status values, such as ACTIVE, PENDING, and CANCELLED
A specific order placed by a specific customer last Tuesday
questions.explain: The list of customers is master data and a specific order is transactional data; the short, stable set of valid status values used to classify those orders is reference data.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say small reference data sets can cause outsized problems when they're wrong?
options: Because a handful of reference rows can be referenced by millions of records across many systems, so damage shows up everywhere at once
Because reference data cannot be backed up like other data types
Because reference data sets are always more complex to query than master data
Because reference data is stored in a different programming language than other data
questions.explain: The asymmetry between a tiny data set and its enormous blast radius — every system referencing that code — is exactly why reference data gets its own governance discipline.
